items: Is the market structure working in the lender’s favor? In our view, the balance of power remains in the hands of the lender. US regional banks remain slow to put capital to work and punitive regulatory capital requirements continue to hamstring financing to Main Street America. As a result, non-bank lenders like BasePoint are able to provide important financing solutions to under-served markets while targeting consistent stable, uncorrelated returns to our clients.

blocks.html: Credit spreads, which had widened modestly during the Q1 bout of risk off sentiment, also round-tripped in Q2. Investment Grade spreads, which were ~90 basis points at the end of Q1, tightened back intothe high-70 basis point range by quarter- end — within the bottom decile of post-financial-crisis readings and in the vicinity of the February 2007 cycle tights. High yield had a similar reaction: HY spreads, which had widened into the 300 – 345 basis point range by the end of Q1, retraced to roughly 260–280 basis points by the end of Q2 (the 20- year average for HY is ~488 basis points). The message from the public credit markets is clear: There is no systemic credit stress; the round-trip suggests the Q1’s moves reflected transient geopolitical risks rather than any deterioration in underlying corporate fundamentals.

blocks.html: Nonetheless, the ebullience of the financial markets was not matched by similarly pristine economic data during Q2. Employment growth, which had cooled in Q1, reaccelerated in Q2, with job gains averaging roughly 175,000 per month across April and May (the unemployment rate held steady at 4.3%!) Inflation, however, began to rise again driven in part by the lagged effects of the energy shock and continuing tariff pass-through. blocks.html: In December 2025, BP PMKN LLC (“BP PMKN”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of BasePoint Capital III LLC, provided interim bridge financing (the “Bridge Financing”) to its wholly owned acquisition vehicle, IPF Parent Holdings Limited (“UK Bidco”) for the pending acquisition of IPF. Under the UK Takeover Code, a bidder must demonstrate that it has sufficient financial resources to implement the offer by the time a firm intention to make an offer is announced. This UK process of a deal’s “cash confirmation” is typically satisfied through committed financing arrangements from banks or other institutions or by having funds readily available (for example, cash on hand or placed in escrow). To satisfy these requirements, BP PMKN funded an escrow account on behalf of UK Bidco in the amount of $549,602,200 to satisfy “cash confirmation” requirements. The funding was documented through two instruments (i) a $274,801,100 USD- denominated note issued by UK Bidco (the “Eurobond”) and (ii) a $274,801,100 secured promissory note issued by BP PMKN. BasePoint expects to refinance the Bridge Financing in full at or shortly prior to the closing of the acquisition. The Fund will have the option, but will not be obligated, to participate in the permanent financing of the acquisition. If the acquisition does not close, the funds in the escrow account will be released from the escrow account and returned to BP PMKN.
